findingsAndDispositions: Reflaxe's generic output cleanup was incompatible with exact ownership; disabled it and made the compiler publish through a content-bound manifest-last owner.
A basename-only module path could collide; replaced it with length-prefixed module and type segments plus duplicate identity/path rejection.
Compiler callback order could not define include order; collected typed static references and topologically ordered the complete graph after lowering.
A floating PHP target would make syntax policy implicit; required the exact php74-modern-v1 profile and added missing/unknown profile negatives.

The first WordPress consumer design could have confused package boot with WordPress compatibility; the package manifest explicitly records wordpressRuntimeCompatibility as not-claimed and the test does not enter the WordPress runtime scorecard.
Cross-process crash journaling, symlink-component confinement, namespaces, and autoloaders are not established by this slice and remain outside the protected claim.
The module graph now treats the generic Int32 helper as a runtime artifact. Source-owned modules declare the helper dependency, and the ordered bootstrap loads it before each consumer.
The php74-modern-v1 manifest now declares minimumIntBits as 64. This field makes the runtime width requirement part of the exact profile contract.
Runtime unary Int negation adds one method to the existing Int32 runtime artifact. It does not add a second runtime owner, change the dependency topology, or broaden the WordPress runtime claim.
Runtime dividend remainder uses the existing application module and native PHP operator. It adds no runtime artifact or dependency edge.
Runtime dividend division adds one method to the existing Int32 runtime artifact. It does not add another runtime owner or dependency edge.
Bool equality changes only source-owned Calculator and Main module bytes. It adds no runtime artifact or dependency edge. The exact new module bytes passed the hosted matrix.
Int inequality and the source-owned Int predicate change only Calculator and Main module bytes. They add no runtime artifact or dependency edge, and the exact new bytes passed the hosted matrix.

String inequality and the source-owned String predicate change only Calculator and Main module bytes. They add no runtime artifact or dependency edge, and the exact new bytes passed the hosted matrix.
String less-than changes only Calculator and Main module bytes. The generated strcmp call adds no runtime artifact or dependency edge, and the exact new bytes passed the hosted matrix.
String less-or-equal changes only Calculator and Main module bytes. The generated strcmp call adds no runtime artifact or dependency edge, and the exact new bytes passed the hosted matrix.
String greater-than changes only Calculator and Main module bytes. The generated strcmp call adds no runtime artifact or dependency edge, and the exact new bytes passed the hosted matrix.
